meta.location: Mulek, Bountiful, and the borders by the east sea
principles: A commander who knows what he cannot do

world_behind.title: The Lamanites wake to a dead king
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has them find Amalickiah dead in his tent and Teancum ready for battle. They abandon the northward march and shut themselves in Mulek.

world_behind.title: Ammoron inherits and holds
world_behind.text: Verse 3 makes the brother king; verse 4 has him order the captured cities kept, because they had cost so much blood.

world_behind.title: Teancum declines the attack twice
world_behind.text: Verses 5 and 17 have him look at the fortifications, judge it impossible, and stop. Mormon records the refusal as sound judgment.

world_behind.title: Moroni's orders arrive by letter
world_behind.text: Verses 8 through 11 give five instructions: hold prisoners, fortify Bountiful, secure the narrow pass, harass the enemy, and retake cities by stratagem if possible.

world_behind.title: Prisoners are held as currency
world_behind.text: Verse 8 says to keep every Lamanite prisoner as a ransom for Nephites taken. Alma 54 and 55 are the negotiation this sets up.

world_behind.title: The Lamanites are fighting on two fronts by design
world_behind.text: Verses 12 and 13 have Ammoron attack by the west sea to draw Nephite forces away while the east-sea garrisons harass.

world_behind.title: The council of war precedes the plan
world_behind.text: Verse 19 has Moroni, Teancum, and many chief captains meet to work out how to draw the Lamanites out. The decoy is a decision taken together.

words.text: Vastness, great size. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible, both in these war chapters. Mormon uses it of the Lamanite numbers, as one of the two reasons Teancum did not attack.

A price paid to free a captive. The word occurs once in this record and thirteen times in the King James Bible, where it usually names what redeems a life. Moroni uses it of prisoners held for exchange.

To wear down by repeated attack. The word occurs four times in this record and never in the King James Bible, three of them in these two chapters. Both sides use the method, and Mormon uses the word of both.
A formal meeting to decide. The phrase council of war occurs once in scripture. Mormon names Moroni, Teancum, and many chief captains, which makes the decoy a decision of the whole command.

Something used to lure an enemy out of position. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible. Mormon uses it here and again in Alma 58, both times of Nephite commanders drawing Lamanites out of forts.
Force, energy. The word occurs three times in this record and never in the King James Bible. Mormon uses it of the Lamanite pursuit, which is the moment the plan is working.

phrases.term: They found Amalickiah was dead in his own tent
phrases.text: The discovery, given from the Lamanite side. Alma 51 ended with Teancum's return; this verse shows the morning, and verse 2 gives the effect: the northward design abandoned.

phrases.term: They had not taken any cities save they had lost much blood
phrases.text: Ammoron's reason for holding what his brother took. The cost already paid becomes the argument for paying more, and it fixes the Lamanite posture for ten chapters.

phrases.term: Teancum thought it was not expedient that he should attempt to attack them in their forts
phrases.text: A commander declining a fight he cannot win. Mormon gives both reasons, the enemy's determination and their numbers, and treats the decision as sound.

phrases.term: He kept his men round about, as if making preparations for war; yea, and truly he was preparing
phrases.text: Mormon corrects the appearance in the same sentence. What looked like a feint was also real work, and the ambiguity is exactly what the position required.

phrases.term: That he should retain all the prisoners of the Lamanites as a ransom
phrases.text: Moroni turns captives into a negotiating position. The instruction is given before any exchange is proposed, and Alma 54 shows it being used.

phrases.term: Secure the narrow pass which led into the land northward
phrases.text: The chokepoint of Alma 50 becomes a standing military objective. Moroni's reason is that losing it would let the Lamanites harass on every side.

phrases.term: That perhaps he might take again by stratagem or some other way those cities
phrases.text: Moroni's own word for the method. He authorizes trickery in an order, which is what verses 21 through 26 then carry out.

phrases.term: I would come unto you, but behold, the Lamanites are upon us in the borders of the land by the west sea
phrases.text: The one line of Moroni's letter Mormon quotes directly. It explains the two-front problem from the Nephite side in a sentence.

phrases.term: That they might by some means flatter them out of their strongholds
phrases.text: The council's stated aim. Flatter here means entice, and the word carries the same sense the record uses of Amalickiah, applied now to a tactic instead of a man.

phrases.term: Moroni, having no hopes of meeting them upon fair grounds
phrases.text: Mormon explains why the decoy was chosen. Jacob refused the open field, so the plan follows a refused invitation to fight on even terms.

phrases.term: They took courage and pursued them with vigor
phrases.text: The Lamanites do the one thing the plan needs. Mormon reports their confidence at the moment it becomes the mechanism of their loss.

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: A new king
verses.text: The Lamanites find Amalickiah dead and Teancum ready, abandon the northward march, and retreat into Mulek. Ammoron, his brother, is made king and orders the captured cities held, because they cost so much blood.

verses.label: v. 5–11
verses.title: Orders from Moroni
verses.text: Teancum judges an attack on the forts inexpedient and builds defenses instead until reinforcements arrive. Moroni sends orders: hold all prisoners as ransom, fortify Bountiful, secure the narrow pass, harass the enemy, retake cities by stratagem if possible, and fortify the cities still held. He cannot come; the west sea has him.

verses.label: v. 12–16
verses.title: Two fronts
verses.text: Ammoron goes to the west sea to draw Nephite forces away, having ordered the eastern garrisons to harass and take what they can. Moroni's men are strengthened. Teancum receives orders to attack Mulek and retake it if possible.

verses.label: v. 17–20
verses.title: The refusal, and the council
verses.text: Teancum sees the fortifications and abandons the attempt, returning to Bountiful to wait for Moroni. Moroni arrives late in the twenty-seventh year. A council of war meets to find a way to draw the Lamanites out. Embassies invite Jacob to the plains, and he refuses.

verses.label: v. 21–26
verses.title: The decoy
verses.text: Moroni resolves on a plan. Teancum takes a small force down the seashore while Moroni marches by night west of Mulek. The guards see Teancum; the Lamanites march out; Teancum retreats northward and is pursued. Moroni takes the city, killing those who will not yield their weapons.

verses.label: v. 27–33
verses.title: The turn
verses.text: The pursuit reaches Bountiful and meets Lehi with fresh men. The Lamanites flee in confusion toward Mulek, weary, and find Moroni waiting. Caught between the two forces, and with Jacob determined to cut through, the fighting becomes desperate.

verses.label: v. 34–40
verses.title: The surrender
verses.text: Moroni is wounded and Jacob is killed. Lehi comes on their rear and the Lamanites, hemmed in, throw down their weapons and plead for mercy. Moroni takes their weapons and their prisoners, and the remainder are delivered up rather than killed.

chapter.title: Two commanders decline the same attack
chapter.text: Teancum in verse 5 and again in verse 17. Mormon records the refusals without criticism, and the chapter's solution is a plan instead of more force.

chapter.title: The orders are quoted as a list
chapter.text: Prisoners, Bountiful, the pass, harassment, stratagem, fortification. Mormon gives Moroni's letter as six concrete instructions and one apology for not coming.

chapter.title: Prisoners become policy before they become leverage
chapter.text: Verse 8 sets the rule; Alma 54 and 55 spend two chapters on the exchange it makes possible.

chapter.title: Both sides are trying to stretch the other
chapter.text: Ammoron opens a second front to draw Nephites west while his garrisons press east. Mormon states the intention plainly in verse 13.

chapter.title: The plan is made in committee
chapter.text: A council of war with many chief captains, then a resolution. The record credits the decoy to a meeting before it credits it to Moroni.

chapter.title: The enemy's courage is the mechanism
chapter.text: The Lamanites take heart at a retreating force and pursue with vigor, and that is what empties the city. Their best moment is the plan working.

chapter.title: Freshness decides the second engagement
chapter.text: Verse 28 says the men of Lehi were fresh and the Lamanites wearied by their march. Mormon tracks the physical state of armies the way he tracks their armor.

chapter.title: The chapter ends in a surrender accepted
chapter.text: Hemmed in, they throw down their weapons and plead, and Moroni takes them prisoner. As in Alma 44, the fighting stops when the other side yields.

applications.title: Decline the attack you cannot win
applications.text: Teancum looked at the forts and stopped. When the direct approach is clearly beyond your means, saying so is a decision rather than a failure.

applications.title: Hold what you will need to trade
applications.text: Moroni ordered prisoners kept before any exchange was on the table. Think ahead about what you may need to offer, and do not spend it early.

applications.title: Secure the chokepoint
applications.text: The narrow pass mattered more than its size. Identify the one place in your situation where losing control would cost you everything else, and hold it.

applications.title: Decide it in council
applications.text: The plan came out of a meeting of captains. When you are stuck, put the problem in front of the people who know the ground, rather than working it out alone.

questions.text: What am I holding on to because of what it already cost me?
What have I been attacking head-on that I should stop attacking?
Where am I preparing in earnest while appearing to?
What have I had to say I cannot come to?
When did someone refuse me fair ground, and what did I do?
What have I pursued with vigor that was leading me away?
